description: Figure 5 is a four-panel composite of mechanical property plots (red curves/markers on a pale blue background) that demonstrates the Bauschinger effect and hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening of the duplex lightweight steel. (a) True stress (MPa, 0-1800) versus true strain (%, 0-12) for a loading-unloading-reloading (LUR) tensile test: six hysteresis loops whose peak stress rises from just above the 1400 MPa gridline near 3% strain to just under the 1800 MPa gridline near 11% strain. (b) Local amplification of the loop at 8.6% true strain (true strain 7.5-9.5%, true stress 0-2200 MPa) with green square markers labelled σu and σr and double-headed arrows labelled σf (twice) and σHDI on the right; the inset magnifies the crossing of the unloading/reloading tangents, whose intersection is labelled σb. (c) Two stacked plots sharing true strain (%, 0-12) as abscissa: hysteresis area (MPa, ticks to 200) and Δσy (MPa, 0-24), both rising monotonically with strain. (d) HDI stress (MPa, 600-850) versus true strain (%), rising monotonically from just above the 600 MPa gridline at ~1% strain to ~845 MPa at ~10.4% strain. Together the panels show that progressive strain accumulation enlarges the hysteresis loops and raises HDI/back stress, producing continuous HDI strengthening.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a LUR true stress-true strain curve with six loading/unloading cycles, plotting true stress (MPa, 0-1800) against true strain (%, 0-12).
Panel (a) shows the peak true stress of each successive cycle rising stepwise until the final loading segment ends just below the 1800 MPa gridline at about 11% true strain.

Panel (b) marks the unloaded yield stress σu near the 400 MPa gridline and the reloaded yield stress σr near the 1200 MPa gridline with green square markers on the unloading and reloading branches of the ~8.6% true-strain loop.
Panel (b) carries double-headed arrows labelled σf (twice) and σHDI on its right-hand side, the σHDI arrow spanning from the σu level to the σr level.

The inset of panel (b) enlarges the region where the extrapolated unloading and reloading tangents cross; the intersection point is labelled σb, while the inset axis tick labels are only partially legible.
Panel (c) is composed of two stacked plots sharing a true strain (%) abscissa from 0 to 12, the upper showing hysteresis area (MPa) and the lower showing Δσy (MPa).

In panel (c) both the hysteresis area and Δσy increase monotonically with true strain over the six data points, the hysteresis area rising from between the 40 and 80 MPa gridlines at ~1% strain to about the 200 MPa gridline at ~10.4% strain.

Panel (d) shows HDI stress (MPa, axis 600-850) increasing monotonically with true strain from just above the 600 MPa gridline at ~1% strain to ~845 MPa at ~10.4% strain, with the steepest segment between ~6.8% and ~8.6% true strain.
The caption states that panel (b) is a local amplification of the hysteresis loop defining σu, σr, σb and Δσy; only σu, σr, σb, σf and σHDI labels could be read in the pixels.

The citing text states that LUR tensile tests were performed with repeated loading/unloading at engineering strains of 1%, 3%, 5%, 7%, 9% and 11%, corresponding to true strains of 1.0%, 2.9%, 4.9%, 6.8%, 8.6% and 10.4%.
The citing text states that Figure 5b shows a typical LUR loop at 8.6% true strain and that HDI stress is calculated as σHDI = (σu + σr)/2 after Yang et al.
The citing text states that the hysteresis area increases with increasing strain, reflecting the Bauschinger effect and HDI strengthening, and that Δσy gradually increases with strain accumulation.

The citing text states that σHDI obtained by extrapolating the HDI stress-strain curve (Figure 5d) is 597 MPa; the plotted points of panel (d) all lie above 600 MPa, so the 597 MPa value is an extrapolated value not directly readable from the pixels.

The citing text attributes the increase in HDI stress to deformation incompatibility between different grains and phases accumulating geometrically necessary dislocations at heterogeneous interfaces, generating back and forward stresses in the soft and hard regions of the austenite/B2 duplex structure.

subfigures.description: True stress (MPa, 0-1800) vs true strain (%, 0-12) LUR tensile curve with six load-unload-reload hysteresis loops; the loop peaks step up from just above the 1400 MPa gridline (near 3% strain) to just below the 1800 MPa gridline (near 11% strain).

Magnified single hysteresis loop at ~8.6% true strain (true strain 7.5-9.5%, true stress 0-2200 MPa) with green square markers labelled σu (near the 400 MPa gridline) and σr (near the 1200 MPa gridline), plus double-headed arrows labelled σf and σHDI; the inset enlarges the tangent-line crossing labelled σb. The printed panel letter is partially cropped and could be misread.

Two stacked plots sharing the true strain (%) abscissa 0-12: upper plot of hysteresis area (MPa, ticks up to 200) and lower plot of Δσy (MPa, 0-24), each with six red data points at ~1.0, 2.9, 4.9, 6.8, 8.6 and 10.4% true strain; both quantities increase monotonically with strain.

HDI stress (MPa, y axis 600-850) vs true strain (%) for six red data points; the curve rises monotonically from just above the 600 MPa gridline at ~1% strain to ~845 MPa at ~10.4% strain, with a steeper rise between ~6.8 and ~8.6% strain.
